parsed_answer.content: In Java, method overriding and method hiding are mechanisms that dictate how subclasses interact with methods defined in their superclasses, but they operate on fundamentally different principles of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides a specific implementation of an instance method already defined in its superclass. This is the cornerstone of polymorphism; the JVM uses dynamic method dispatch (invokevirtual) to determine at runtime which method implementation to execute based on the actual object type, not the reference type. Conversely, method hiding occurs when a subclass defines a static method with the same signature as a static method in the superclass. Because static methods are bound at compile-time (invokestatic), they do not participate in polymorphic behavior. Instead, the method is 'hidden' by the subclass implementation, and the compiler binds the call to the method associated with the reference type, not the underlying object instance.

items: Overriding requires the @Override annotation to ensure the compiler verifies the signature matches exactly, preventing accidental overloading instead of overriding.

Hiding is strictly tied to the class scope; if you cast an object to the superclass type, the hidden method of the superclass will be invoked, whereas an overridden method would still trigger the subclass logic.

The JVM's invokevirtual instruction performs a lookup in the virtual method table (vtable) of the actual object instance for overriding, whereas invokestatic resolves the method reference directly from the constant pool based on the declared type.

parsed_answer.content: A common production trap is assuming static methods can be overridden. If you are writing a library and rely on static methods for utility logic, you cannot use polymorphism to swap behaviors. If you find yourself needing to 'override' static behavior, you are likely violating the Liskov Substitution Principle and should refactor the logic into an instance-based Strategy pattern or use a Factory pattern to inject the correct implementation.

title: What is method hiding vs method overriding?
